A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LVAgent and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A-C. All substantive material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark accuracy, efficiency experiments and ablations, including four-agent results in Appendix B.3.

after.justification: v5 retains the original benchmark, efficiency and ablation results, including the additional experiments in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1-3.5 retain the same selection, ASP-CLIP retrieval, action, reflection and multi-round collaboration procedures. Appendix C's operational prompts are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use the same five-source LongVR training mixture and evaluate on EgoSchema, VideoMME, MLVU and LongVideoBench, with the same subtitle conditions.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark and efficiency tables and the retrieval/discussion comparisons. Newly cited works in v5 are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The benchmark splits, metrics, sampling procedures, model teams and training settings match. Both retain temperature 0.01, a 168-token generation limit, batch size 64 and 10 training epochs, alongside the same Appendix B evaluation settings.

E4.justification: Both contain the same component, agent-count, discussion-round, retrieval-model, discussion-method and threshold ablations. The qualitative examples and Appendix B's efficiency and four-agent analyses are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both use the same point-estimate reporting without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged. Table 1 retains LVAgent scores of 82.9 on EgoSchema, 80.0 on LongVideoBench, 83.9 on MLVU and 81.7/86.6 on VideoMME without/with subtitles. Appendix B's timing and four-agent results also match.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(8) and their mathematical definitions remain equivalent. No assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same novelty claim for dynamic multi-MLLM collaboration and the same benchmark accuracy and superiority claims.

C2.justification: The explanations involving complementary agent strengths, iterative refinement and retrieval thresholds are unchanged. Appendix B.3 retains the same accuracy-versus-time rationale for choosing three agents; no new limitation or applicability qualification appears.

D1.justification: Both supply the same code link, hyperparameters, PyTorch and eight-A800-80G hardware information, runtime breakdown, dataset construction details, task-specific agent teams and prompt templates.

R1.justification: v5 adds seven cited works, including Super encoding network, Videochat-m1 and UniFlow, mainly by extending existing citation lists. The substantive positioning relative to prior video models and agent approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 condenses part of the Long Video Agent discussion and moves the Method heading after that discussion, placing the survey within Related Work. Author-footnote formatting receives small edits; most prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-7 and Tables 1-9 retain their content and basic designs. Caption spacing, text placement, prompt-table row spacing and bibliography flow show limited typesetting changes.

improvement.justification: v5 modestly improves organization by placing the Long Video Agent survey within Related Work and starting Method at the method description, while reducing repetitive wording. The gains concern clarity and navigation; the scientific evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
